title: Commercial and Market Access
answer: Commercial teams were early adopters of AI agents: CRM vendors built life sciences agents for field sales and medical liaisons, and several of the largest drugmakers chose new AI based engagement platforms in 2025 and 2026. AI is also used to analyse real world evidence for market access.

reading.body:
Commercial teams in pharma adopted AI agents before most other functions, and the largest drugmakers consolidated on shared platforms rather than building their own.

The pattern is consolidation. Novartis and AstraZeneca both selected Salesforce Agentforce Life Sciences in December 2025, and Chiesi Group followed in April 2026. Salesforce reported more than 140 life sciences organizations on the same product. Field sales, medical liaisons, and customer engagement are the entry point, with real world evidence analysis for market access close behind.

This matters for AI because it shows where regulated industries actually deploy agents first. The constraint is not model capability but review. Promotional content and interactions with health care professionals fall under the same medical, legal, and regulatory approval whether a person or an agent produces them, so the winning vendors are the ones that put that review inside the workflow.

The data covers platform choices and adoption counts, not outcomes. It does not say whether these deployments improved sales, reduced cost, or shortened review cycles, and it does not cover the compute or infrastructure behind them.

sections.heading: What it means for a commercial team

siblings.name: AI Adoption and Governance in Life Sciences

explainer:
Commercial work in life sciences covers how medicines and devices reach the people who prescribe, buy and pay for them: field sales and medical liaison teams who meet doctors, marketing to health care professionals and patients, and market access teams who show payers and health technology assessment bodies that a product is worth its price.

All of it is regulated. Promotional claims must match the approved label, be balanced with safety information, and pass medical, legal and regulatory review before use. Interactions with health care professionals are logged and governed by codes of practice. That framework applies just as much when an AI system drafts an email, suggests a talking point or answers a doctor's question.

AI has spread quickly here. Customer relationship management systems used by pharma now include AI agents that brief representatives, recommend next actions and draft follow ups, and several of the largest drugmakers have adopted them since 2025. A safer class of external tools answers questions using only content already approved through review. Analytics teams use AI on real world data and health economics to support pricing and access, and competitive intelligence teams use it to track rivals' pipelines.

The risk is unapproved claims reaching doctors or patients. Companies that build review into the workflow, and keep humans accountable for what goes out, get the benefit without the compliance exposure.
key_points: Promotional rules apply to anything an AI drafts or says externally.
Agentic CRM is now standard among large drugmakers.
Closed systems that answer only with approved content are the safe external pattern.
AI supports health economics, real world evidence and competitive intelligence.
Build medical, legal and regulatory review into AI workflows from the start.
